title: 2024 AMC 8 Problem 15
statement: Let the letters \(F,\) \(L,\) \(Y,\) \(B,\) \(U,\) \(G\) represent distinct digits. Suppose \(\text{FLYFLY}\) is the greatest number that satisfies the equation \[ 8 \cdot \text{FLYFLY} = \text{BUGBUG}. \] What is the value of \(\text{FLY} + \text{BUG}?\)

solutions.text:
Firstly, note that \[\text{FLYFLY} = 1001(\text{FLY})\] and, similarly, \[\text{BUGBUG}=1001(\text{BUG})\] so the equation can be simplified to \(8 \cdot \text{FLY} = \text{BUG}.\)

Because \(\text{BUG}\) has three digits, \(\text{FLY}\le124.\) The largest possible three-digit number at most \(124\) with distinct digits is \(124,\) but \(8\cdot124=992\) repeats a digit and also reuses the digit \(2.\)

The next candidate is \(123,\) and \(8\cdot123=984.\) The six digits \(1,\) \(2,\) \(3,\) \(9,\) \(8,\) and \(4\) are all distinct, so \(123\) is the greatest possible value of \(\text{FLY}.\)

Hence, \[ \begin{gathered} \text{FLY} + \text{BUG} = 123 + 984 \\ = 1107. \end{gathered} \]

Thus, C is the correct answer.
